newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese solar cell makers plan production jumps.
newsitem.headline: Japanese solar cell makers plan production jumps.

text.p: Japanese solar cell makers, such as Sharp Corp and Sanyo Electric Co Ltd, are rushing to boost production, mainly in response to growing demand for solar power-generating systems for houses.
Sharp announced on Friday that it would invest seven billion yen to construct the world's largest solar cell factory, which is scheduled to start production in April 1998.
The factory will have an initial annual production capacity of 20 megawatts, but that could eventually be increased to 150 megawatts, a company statement said.
A regular solar power system for a household of four has the capacity to generate about three kilowatts.
The company will not only manufacture solar cells for home use, but also for use on satellites.
Sanyo Electric plans to boost its annual production capacity of solar batteries to 20 megawatts from 15 megawatts by the end of March 1998 and to 60 megawatts by 2000.
Sanyo plans to spend 2.5 billion yen to build a new factory at its U.S. subsidiary Solec International Inc, and a new production line at its factory in Hyogo prefecture in western Japan.
"We've decided to make these investments to step up production as household-use demand (for solar power) is increasing," Yasuo Ohira, a Sanyo managing director.
The company purchased Solec International in November 1994.

Meanwhile, Kyocera Corp said it expects to complete a new production line at its Shiga factory in western Japan in October which will more than double its capacity to make solar batteries to 30 megawatts.
The company also aims to further raise the production capacity to 60 megawatts by 2000, an official at Kyocera's solar system marketing unit said.
"Solar systems for homes have become more popular as prices have fallen considerably in the last several years," a Kyocera official said.
A home solar system cost about six million yen when Kyocera first entered the business in December 1993, he said, but that is now down to about 3.2 million to 3.3 million yen.

Sales have also been helped by a government subsidy programme, under which the government pays about one-third of the cost of a home solar system. The government plans to increase by more than five times to 9,400 homes in the current fiscal year, a government official said.
